name: whoami
title: Who am I
description: Show the identity Pyre authenticates you as (an agent session or the owner).

name: list_nodes
title: List machines
description: List machines with connectivity, harnesses and load. Offline does not mean idle.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

name: list_models
title: List models
description: List the models and reasoning efforts each machine's agent harnesses offer, for start_session model and effort (any name the harness accepts also works).

harness.description: only this harness: claude, codex or agy

name: list_sessions
title: List sessions
description: List sessions across the fleet: one line each with id, title, run state, machine ("this machine" shares your filesystem), age and project.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

include_monitors.description: include monitor sessions (pyre monitor add); by default each session shows only how many monitors watch for it

node.description: node ID (node_...) or name; default: this session's node

project.description: project ID/name, or "none" for standalone sessions

name: get_session
title: Show session
description: Get one session with its current run, capabilities, lease and pending approvals.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: start_session
title: Start session
description: Start a peer session on a machine (no project needed). Waits up to 20 s; a failed launch is an error. It messages you automatically when it finishes a turn (with its last message), needs input, or exits; no need to ask it to.

account.description: explicit account: ID, label or rota name, or a unique prefix; at its limit the best eligible account is used instead (with a note) unless strict_account

branch.description: branch for the fresh worktree (default pyre/<slug of the prompt or title>)

cwd.description: absolute working directory on the node

effort.description: reasoning effort: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (codex also ultra); default: the harness's own

env_file.description: absolute path on the node to KEY=VALUE lines added to the harness environment at every launch (a private file: chmod 600; Pyre and login keys refused unless empty); only the path is recorded

fallback_harness.description: claude: when no Codex (OpenAI) account is free, run on Claude instead; use for reviews and second opinions. Default: a Codex launch with no free account fails at once with the reason

fresh.description: start in a new worktree and branch of repo instead of its main checkout

harness.description: claude, codex, agy or shell (agy: Google Antigravity, on machines that have it)

harness_args.description: extra harness flags from an allowlist, e.g. claude --append-system-prompt-file=F, --plugin-dir=D, --dangerously-load-development-channels=plugin:N@M; kept across resumes; Pyre-controlled flags are refused

model.description: model (default: the harness's own); claude takes opus/sonnet/haiku/fable or a full name; choices per machine: list_models

native_resume.description: claude: continue this existing conversation (session id) started outside Pyre; stop its process first

node.description: node ID (node_...) or name; default: the least loaded connected node with the harness (with project+repo: among nodes holding that checkout; with cwd: this session's node); the result's placement says which and why

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

permissions.description: ask (approval prompts) or bypass (no approval prompts, no sandbox); default: the node's setting

repo.description: with project: project repo ID (its recorded checkout, or the worktree source); without project: a repository name from the repo index, fuzzy-matched (the machine defaults to where it exists, the harness to claude, the directory to its main checkout)

report_to_parent.description: report back to the starting session automatically (default true when a session starts it; false turns it off)

repos.description: several repository names from the repo index: fresh worktrees of each on one branch in ~/pyre-work/<slug>/

strict_account.description: keep account even when it is at its limit or ineligible (the launch fails)

worktree.description: branch for an isolated git worktree

name: read_session
title: Read transcript
description: Read a session's bounded, redacted transcript. Use next_cursor to continue.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: interrupt_session
title: Interrupt session
description: Interrupt a session's current turn (for an idle Codex session, also stop the background commands it left running). The receipt reports acceptance; the outcome is observed separately.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: stop_session
title: Stop session
description: Stop a session's current run (the session stays resumable).

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: send_message
title: Send message
description: Send a durable message to a session, "owner", channel:<name> or project; reply_to alone replies to its sender. delivery_status.summary says if it gets through. A report to the owner that asks nothing is an update, not in his inbox.

attach.description: published IDs: ver_..., rev_..., note_... (not file paths)

info.description: store only; never inject into a runtime

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

request_ack.description: ask the recipient to acknowledge (to the owner: keeps a report in his inbox)

name: inbox
title: Inbox
description: List unacked messages addressed to this session (or a given mailbox), one line each; get_message <id> shows a full body. wait_seconds long-polls for new mail.

after_cursor.description: only messages after this inbox cursor

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

session.description: mailbox: session ref or "owner" (default: this session)

unacked.description: only messages without ack/reply (default true for an inbox; false lists handled mail too)

name: wait_reply
title: Wait for reply
description: Wait for a reply to a message you sent. Times out with an error saying whether your message is still queued and why; returns at once if the recipient ended or was archived.

name: get_message
title: Show message
description: Show a message: sender, thread, state and full body (format json adds every delivery fact and receipt). Indeterminate means unknown, not failed.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

name: ack_message
title: Acknowledge message
description: Acknowledge a message without replying.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: reissue_message
title: Reissue message
description: Re-send uncertain or rejected work as a new message referencing the original. Requires accept_duplicate_risk=true; never use as a blind retry.

accept_duplicate_risk.description: must be true: the recipient may act twice

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: resolve_delivery
title: Resolve delivery
description: Record a decision (accepted or rejected) about an indeterminate delivery after inspecting evidence.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: list_approvals
title: List approvals
description: List pending approvals/questions (all states with all=true).

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: answer_approval
title: Answer approval
description: Answer an approval by ID; the answer is bound to the approval's own run and refused if stale.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: list_projects
title: List projects
description: List projects (optional shared workspaces).

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

name: create_project
title: Create project
description: Create a project (an optional shared workspace). Only name is required; repos and checkouts are optional.

brief.description: brief text; becomes the brief document

checkouts.description: checkouts as node:/abs/path:repo:mode[:branch] (mode shared|worktree|plain; repo is one of repos)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: archive_session
title: Archive session
description: When your work is finished and reported, archive yourself with archive_session (no arguments); a live one archives when its turn ends; sessions under it go with it. Sessions outside your tree go to the owner for approval (approval_ask).

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID or exact title (default: yourself)

name: archive_project
title: Archive project
description: Archive a project. Live sessions in it refuse unless with_sessions: true, which archives its ended sessions now and its live ones when their turns end.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

with_sessions.description: also archive the project's sessions (live ones when their turns end)

name: associate_session_project
title: Associate session with project
description: Attach an existing session to a project, or detach it with none=true.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: list_documents
title: List documents
description: List versioned documents (optionally in a project).

name: get_document
title: Read document
description: Read a document (head or a revision). Note revision_id: pass it as base_revision when proposing an edit.

document.description: document ID, or slug with project

name: propose_document
title: Propose document revision
description: Propose a successor revision. Commits only if the head is still base_revision; otherwise returns a conflict and preserves your text as a proposal.

document.description: document ID, or slug with project

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: publish
title: Publish artifact
description: Publish a local file as an immutable, durable artifact version. Returns the receipt; a local path alone is not shared.

artifact_id.description: publish a new version of this artifact

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: list_artifacts
title: List artifacts
description: List published artifacts.

session.description: session ID (ses_...), exact title, or "self"

name: comment
title: Comment
description: Comment on an exact artifact version (ver_...) or document revision (rev_...).

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: list_comments
title: List comments
description: List review comments for a version, revision, artifact (art_...) or document (doc_...).

name: create_note
title: Record note
description: Record a note, handoff or decision in shared memory. Put pointers (version/note IDs, branches) in handoffs.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: get_context
title: Launch context
description: Get the bounded launch context: current project brief plus retrieval pointers.

name: memory_search
title: Search memory
description: Search shared memory (transcripts, notes, decisions) with provenance and freshness.

node.description: node ID (node_...) or name; default: this session's node

name: audit_log
title: Audit log
description: Audit log, newest first: account chosen per run and why, automatic account switches (from/to, usage, reason), re-auth, cooldowns, tokens, session starts/stops/renames by whom, machines and upgrades. Read-only; no secrets.

kind.description: only account, session or fleet events

session.description: only this session (ID or exact title)

since.description: how far back: 24h (default), 90m, 7d, an RFC 3339 time, or all

name: connection_check
title: Check connection
description: Check whether you may use a named connection now and where it is available. Connections verified on your node, or for remote use on another, need no grant. Never returns credentials.

session.description: session ID; default: you

name: connection_invoke
title: Use connection
description: Run a read operation on a connection (GitHub, Linear, ...); no grant needed for connections your machines hold. The holding node runs it via Outfit; the credential never reaches you. Writes are refused.

node.description: executing node; default: the hub routes to the verified holder

operation.description: operation name (see the connection's skill or `outfit describe`)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: get_digest
title: While you were away
description: Catch the owner up: per-agent digest since they last looked, ranked needs-you, done, working: what each did, files/docs/artifacts/messages, blockers, a pyre:// link per line. Read-only.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

since.description: "last" (the owner's last-seen mark on this machine, else 12h; default), a duration such as 2h, 90m or 1d, or an RFC 3339 time

name: search
title: Search everything
description: Find past work: search every session transcript on every machine, plus memory, notes and docs. Hits give session, run and seq; read_session with cursor seq-1 opens the turn. Matches are marked « ».

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

node.description: search one machine only (name or ID)

query.description: words to find (all must match; "quoted phrase" for exact)

since.description: only newer matches: 7d, 36h, 90m or a date

sources.description: limit to: transcript, memory, note, document, artifact

name: ask_owner
title: Ask the owner
description: Ask the owner to decide (top-level sessions only). find_asks first. Plenty of context (the owner decides from it alone), 2–4 options each with a detail, a default you will take (none if irreversible); keep working. Same topic_key merges.

action.description: the go-ahead asked for in one word (merge, deploy); a standing grant for exactly this action answers at once when the ask offers its option and has a default

confirm_new.description: create it even though a similar open ask exists under another topic

context.description: markdown, at least 300 characters: what is being decided and why now; what is known or was tried (links, paths); what each option leads to; what happens by default if nobody answers

deadline_minutes.description: default 60; a deadline at night moves to the owner's morning unless urgent

default.description: option id (or label) applied at the deadline if the owner does not answer; omit for irreversible actions

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

irreversible.description: cannot be undone: never answered by a standing grant (give no default)

items.description: batch several like decisions into one ask (e.g. the PRs to merge): the options apply to each item; the owner answers per item or all at once

detail.description: one line: what and why, its state

label.description: what the item is, a few words

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

detail.description: required, one line: what happens if chosen

id.description: short stable id (default a, b, c, d)

project.description: project ID or name (default: this session's project)

reopen.description: ask again on a decided topic because something changed (say what in context)

topic_key.description: short stable slug for the decision, e.g. "auth-token-storage"; the same key merges into the open ask instead of new mail, and a decided topic returns its answer

urgent.description: needs an answer even at night (keeps the deadline)

name: find_asks
title: Find asks
description: Find open asks and those decided in the last 7 days by topic key or text, before asking or messaging the owner. A decided topic is final: act on its answer instead of asking again.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

include_decided.description: include asks decided in the last 7 days (default true)

query.description: text over title, context and options

name: withdraw_ask
title: Withdraw ask
description: Take back your open ask (no longer needed), or mark it superseded by another ask. To correct or add to an ask, call ask_owner again with the same topic_key instead.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: flag_attention
title: Flag for the owner
description: Mark this session "needs you" with a one-line reason, for what only the owner can decide or provide (not progress). Clears when the owner engages, you call clear_attention, or the run ends.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

text.description: one-line reason the owner sees, e.g. "pick a schema: A or B"

name: clear_attention
title: Clear flag
description: Clear this session's own "needs you" flag (for example, you resolved it yourself).

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: propose_grant
title: Propose a standing grant
description: Ask the owner to approve a lasting go-ahead (e.g. merge PRs once reviewed and green). Files an owner ask; only if he approves does Pyre record it, quoting his own answer. Never claim he already said it.

action.description: the go-ahead in one word: merge, ... (asks must name exactly this action to be answered)

deadline_minutes.description: minutes until the proposal expires unanswered (default 1440); nothing is recorded then

expires_days.description: days after approval until it lapses (default 7, max 30)

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

note.description: informational note shown with it, e.g. "once reviewed and CI green" (Pyre never checks it)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

option.description: the ask option (id or label) the grant picks, e.g. merge

scope.description: project (default when this session has one) or session (this session and the sessions it starts)

session.description: scope session: the root of the tree (default: this session; or a session you started)

why.description: why the owner should approve it, with the evidence (his earlier message or ask, links); shown as your words, never as his

name: propose_fact
title: Propose a project fact
description: Ask the owner to approve a settled fact for this project's fact sheet (every new session reads it). Files an owner ask; only if he approves does Pyre add it, quoting his own answer.

deadline_minutes.description: minutes until the proposal expires unanswered (default 1440); nothing is recorded then

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

why.description: why the owner should approve it, with the evidence (his earlier message or ask, links); shown as your words, never as his

name: list_grants
title: List standing grants
description: List the standing grants (the owner's lasting go-aheads) that hold for this session: its project's and its session tree's.

all.description: every grant you may see, not only those holding for this session

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

session.description: list the grants holding for this session (default: this session)

name: revoke_grant
title: Revoke a standing grant
description: Revoke a standing grant that holds for you, e.g. when the owner takes the go-ahead back. Asks for its action then go to the owner again.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

name: report_issue
title: Report a Pyre or machine problem
description: Report Pyre misbehaving (pyre_bug), a broken machine (machine) or wrong/confusing Pyre instructions (guidance), with evidence. Not for your own mistakes or the project's build/test failures. Keep working around it.

body.description: what you did, what happened, what you expected; evidence (exact errors, IDs, commands) in markdown

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

node.description: the machine a machine issue is about (default: yours)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

related.description: session or run IDs involved (yours are added automatically)

title.description: the problem in one line ("send_message to a stopped session reported delivered")

annotations.title: Report a Pyre or machine problem

name: list_issues
title: List issues
description: List issues sessions reported (Pyre bugs, machine problems, guidance problems), most recently seen first. Default: open and triaged.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

status.description: open, triaged, fixed, wontfix or duplicate, comma-separated, or all (default: open,triaged)

name: get_issue
title: Show an issue
description: Show an issue with its reports (each with its evidence and context) and triage notes.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

name: update_issue
title: Triage an issue
description: Triage session or owner only: set an issue's status (fixed, wontfix, duplicate close it), add a note or links (PR URLs).

duplicate_of.description: with status duplicate: the issue it duplicates (later reports go there)

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

note.description: what was found or done (shown as the resolution when closing)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

status.description: open, triaged, fixed, wontfix or duplicate

name: update_project_page
title: Update project page
description: Update your project's page (leads only): the markdown page and/or its status card (progress, phase, in flight, ready for the owner, shipped). Create it early; update the card at each milestone. Stale after 30 idle min while work runs.

base_revision_id.description: revision you edited (get_project_page); a newer page then fails instead of being replaced

content.description: the whole page in markdown (replaces the previous version); omit to update only the status

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

project.description: project ID or name (default: this session's project)

status.description: the status card; replaces the previous one (send every field you want kept; get_project_page shows the current card)

session.description: session ID doing or owning it

state.description: e.g. review, ci failing, merged, deployed, released

eta.description: when you expect to finish (free text)

in_flight.description: work under way that live sessions do not show by themselves

session.description: session ID doing or owning it

state.description: e.g. review, ci failing, merged, deployed, released

phase.description: one line: where things stand now

ready_for_owner.description: waiting on the owner but not an ask: PRs to review or merge, a build to try

session.description: session ID doing or owning it

state.description: e.g. review, ci failing, merged, deployed, released

shipped.description: merged, deployed or released items (state says which)

session.description: session ID doing or owning it

state.description: e.g. review, ci failing, merged, deployed, released

name: get_project_page
title: Show project page
description: Read your project's page (the owner's view of the project in the web app), with its revision ID for update_project_page.

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

project.description: project ID or name (default: this session's project)

name: waiting_on
title: Waiting on own job
description: Before ending your turn while your own CI, review, workers or watcher are pending: your parent hears you wait (not idle), and again if not woken by expect_minutes. quiet: it hears nothing now; end your turn, don't poll inbox.

expect_minutes.description: when it should be done (default 60, max 1440)

format.description: text (default): compact lines with the ids you need; json: the full structured result

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

quiet.description: don't report this turn's end to your parent; a Monitor, a child's report or a message wakes you (it still hears if you are not woken by expect_minutes, and when your run exits)

what.description: the job, with its URL, e.g. "CI on PR #12 https://github.com/o/r/pull/12"

name: rename_session
title: Rename session
description: Rename any session (default your own) so the owner can tell the work apart, e.g. your own or sessions you started ("Fix stripe webhook retries"). Short, specific, at most ~6 words. A title the owner chose is kept.

icon.description: optional: also set the session's emoji (one emoji; "" clears)

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID or exact title; "self" (default) is your own session

name: set_session_icon
title: Set session icon
description: Give a session (default your own) an emoji shown before its title that reflects its work, e.g. 🐛 for a bug fix, 🚀 for a release. One emoji; "" clears it.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

session.description: session ID or exact title; "self" (default) is your own session

name: reparent_session
title: Reparent session
description: Move sessions under another parent: their end-of-turn reports go there from now on; both sides get a Pyre message. A coordinator can hand its agents to leads; a lead can adopt agents in its project.

operation_id.description: optional stable ID; repeating a call with the same ID returns the original result instead of acting twice

parent.description: new parent: session ID, exact title, or "self"; "" or "none" = top level

session.description: session to move: ID, exact title, or "self" (default: your own session)

sessions.description: several sessions to move to the same parent (IDs or exact titles)
